newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean opposition rejects debate over labour law.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean opposition rejects debate over labour law.

text.p: South Korea's two main opposition parties will not accept an offer to reopen parliamentary debate over a controversial labour law unless it is revoked first, an opposition spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

Park Sun-sook of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics told Reuters that the decision was made at a meeting of senior officials of her party and the smaller United Liberal Democratic Party.
"Any debate in parliament must be made on the condition that the law is made null and void," Park said.
President Kim Young-sam, in a dramatic concession, agreed to revise the law and asked leaders of his ruling New Korea Party and the two opposition parties to reopen parliamentary debate over the law.

National Congress leader Kim Dae-jung on Tuesday called the offer "some progress" but Park said the two opposition parties would continue a campaign to collect 10 million signatures to back their demands for scrapping the law.

As part of his climbdown the president criticised his own party for delaying recognition of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions. The law, rammed through parliament on December 26, bans the confederation until 2000.
